questions.scenario: The school's Annual Day Drama is announced. What is your immediate reaction?

options.A: I want the lead role where I can shout my dialogues loudly so even the back row can hear me.
options.B: I ask for the script to understand the deep backstory of why my character is angry in Scene 3.
options.C: I practice my crying and smiling faces in the mirror to make sure I look perfect on stage.
options.D: I mentally decide which of my classmates fits which role and tell the teacher my suggestions.

questions.scenario: Your friends ask you to do a mimicry of the strict Math teacher during recess. How do you do it?

options.A: I exaggerate their walking style, use loud hand gestures, and make the whole classroom laugh.
options.B: I carefully observe their exact vocabulary, the way they hold the chalk, and their subtle eye twitches.
options.C: I focus heavily on copying their exact facial expressions and the way they raise their eyebrows.
options.D: I don't act, but I force my funniest friend to do it and judge who in the group does the best impression.

questions.scenario: Your group is participating in an inter-school Nukkad Natak (Street Play) competition. What is your role?

options.A: I am standing in the center, singing loudly, clapping with massive energy, and jumping around.
options.B: I research the social issue (like pollution or traffic rules) to make sure our dialogues are logically accurate.
options.C: I focus on holding dramatic emotional pauses, making sure the crowd feels the pain in my expressions.
options.D: I gather the crowd, shout the introductory lines, and make sure everyone enters the circle exactly on cue.

questions.scenario: You are watching a Bollywood blockbuster movie on TV with your family. What catches your attention?

options.A: The high-energy dance numbers and the loud, dramatic dialogue delivery of the hero.
options.B: The villain's complex psychology and trying to understand why they became evil in the first place.
options.C: The hero's perfectly timed single tear, jawline, and how good the lighting looks on their face.
options.D: The chemistry between the actors, making me wonder how they auditioned and selected this exact pair.

questions.scenario: A relative asks you to 'perform something' at a big family wedding function. How do you handle it?

options.A: I immediately launch into a full-energy Salman Khan or Allu Arjun dialogue with action moves.
options.B: I think about my funny uncle's behavior and do an exact, highly observant parody of him.
options.C: I do a dramatic Shah Rukh Khan pose, making sure my eyes look deeply romantic for the camera.
options.D: I redirect the attention by turning into the host, grabbing the mic, and making my younger cousins dance.

questions.scenario: Your class has to make a short video project for Social Studies. What do you volunteer for?

options.A: I want to be the main news anchor, speaking loudly and enthusiastically into the microphone.
options.B: I spend hours writing the script, making sure the character's motivations and historical facts are perfect.
options.C: I make sure the sunlight hits my face perfectly, my hair is set, and my smile looks natural on screen.
options.D: I hold the camera, tell my friends exactly where to stand, and direct the whole shoot like a boss.

questions.scenario: You are feeling very emotional after a massive argument with your sibling. What do you do next?

options.A: I yell dramatic, filmy dialogues like 'You have ruined my life!' just for the theatrical effect.
options.B: I sit quietly and analyze exactly why I am feeling this way, keeping mental notes of real sadness.
options.C: I literally go to the bathroom mirror to look at myself crying and see how my face looks when sad.
options.D: I go to my parents, present both sides of the story objectively, and manage to get my sibling scolded.

questions.scenario: During a proxy period, the class is playing Dumb Charades. What is your strategy?

options.A: I aggressively act out the movie using huge physical movements, jumping, and running across the front.
options.B: I carefully pick out the most logical, obscure hints to explain the movie without moving much.
options.C: I rely completely on subtle, intense facial expressions to convey the exact emotion of the movie title.
options.D: I act as the referee, keeping the score on the blackboard, setting the timer, and catching cheaters.

questions.scenario: Someone is telling a very boring story during the lunch break. How do you react?

options.A: I interrupt them and retell the same story with 10x more energy, voice modulation, and sound effects.
options.B: I ask them deep psychological questions like 'But what was their actual motivation for doing that?'
options.C: I practice my acting skills by giving perfect facial reactions (gasping, smiling) even though I'm bored.
options.D: I smoothly change the topic and point to the funniest person in the group, telling them to speak instead.

questions.scenario: When you dream about the entertainment industry, what is your ultimate goal?

options.A: Performing live in a packed auditorium and hearing the thunderous clapping of the live audience.
options.B: Being recognized as a genius who can completely transform their voice and body for any complex role.
options.C: Seeing my face on a massive cinema screen, delivering a flawless emotional scene that makes people cry.
options.D: Discovering a new superstar and putting together the perfect cast for the biggest blockbuster of the year.

Stage_Actor.title: Stage Actor / Theatre Performer
Stage_Actor.primary_match_text: The Live Energy Bomb! You thrive on live audiences, loud dialogue delivery, and high-energy physical acting.
Stage_Actor.day_in_the_life: Rehearsing in large auditoriums, doing voice projection exercises, performing in Nukkad Nataks (street plays), and feeding off the real-time clapping and energy of a live crowd.
Stage_Actor.alternative_match_text: Voice-Over Artist, Live Anchor, Stand-up Comedian
Stage_Actor.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th (Any Stream) -> Bachelor of Performing Arts (BPA) or BA in Theatre -> Audition for the prestigious National School of Drama (NSD) in Delhi -> Join a professional theatre group.

Method_Actor.title: Method Actor / Character Researcher
Method_Actor.primary_match_text: The Deep Observer! You are highly analytical and love diving deep into a character's psychology and background.
Method_Actor.day_in_the_life: Reading scripts multiple times, observing strangers on local trains to copy their body language, maintaining a character journal, and completely transforming your personality for a role.
Method_Actor.alternative_match_text: Script Consultant, Drama Teacher, Character Writer
Method_Actor.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th (Any Stream) -> BA (Arts/Literature) or BPA -> Acting diploma from Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune or NSD -> Attending intensive method acting workshops.

Screen_Actor.title: Screen Actor / Expression Artist
Screen_Actor.primary_match_text: The Camera Magician! You understand angles, aesthetics, and the power of subtle facial expressions.
Screen_Actor.day_in_the_life: Acting in front of large camera crews, perfectly catching your 'mark' on set, focusing on micro-expressions for close-up shots, and working closely with makeup and lighting departments.
Screen_Actor.alternative_match_text: Model, Television Actor, Digital Content Creator
Screen_Actor.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th (Any Stream) -> Degree in Mass Media / BMM or any Graduation -> Acting courses from institutes like Whistling Woods International or Actor Prepares -> Giving regular screen tests in Mumbai.

Casting_Director.title: Casting Director / Theatre Manager
Casting_Director.primary_match_text: The Master Organizer! You love the chaos of the entertainment world but prefer managing it and finding the right talent.
Casting_Director.day_in_the_life: Holding hundreds of auditions, reading scripts to understand which actor fits best, managing backstage drama during a play, and coordinating with the director to run the show smoothly.
Casting_Director.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th (Any Stream) -> Bachelor of Mass Media (BMM) or BA in Mass Communication -> Assisting casting agencies in Mumbai -> Building a strong network in the film and television industry.
